scenes.text: Almost every cell has its own tiny power plant
scenes.caption: Inside almost every cell in your body are structures called mitochondria that generate energy.

scenes.text: They turn food into usable energy
scenes.caption: Mitochondria convert nutrients and oxygen into ATP, the molecule cells use to power their activities.

scenes.text: Busy cells pack in more of them
scenes.caption: Heart and muscle cells contain thousands of mitochondria because they demand so much energy.
Mitochondria generate the energy that keeps your cells running.

scenes.text: They carry their own tiny genome
scenes.caption: Mitochondria have their own small set of DNA, separate from the DNA stored in the cell's nucleus.
Scientists believe mitochondria descend from ancient bacteria engulfed by early cells over a billion years ago.
Mitochondria generate the energy that keeps your cells running.
Mitochondria convert food and oxygen into the energy that powers nearly everything your cells do.
